comparison: Perfect agreement. Both OpenEval and peer reviewers fully support the core MIC findings (C1, C12-C25) showing magnesium-induced antibiotic resistance. Peer reviewers explicitly state the study 'produced convincing evidence' and OpenEval notes the data are 'internally consistent' with 'substantial and reproducible' effects.

Strong agreement on metabolomics findings. Both support claims C2, C26-C38, C136-C137 regarding fatty acid changes and palmitic acid as a biomarker. OpenEval emphasizes the comprehensive GC-MS methodology and functional validation. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm 'the significance of fatty acid biosynthesis pathway behind the resistance mechanism.' Note: OpenEval R2 includes additional claims (C61-C70, C155-C156, C160-C161, C162) that peer R2 also addresses.

Both address LC-MS fatty acid quantification (C61-C70, C155-C156). OpenEval R7 treats these as confirmatory data with higher resolution than GC-MS. Peer R2 groups these fatty acid measurements with the broader metabolomics findings, supporting them as part of the overall fatty acid biosynthesis evidence.

Strong agreement on functional validation experiments (C3-C4, C71-C74, C157). Both support the exogenous fatty acid supplementation experiments and LC-MS uptake confirmation. OpenEval notes the dose-dependent effects strengthen causality. Peer reviewers indicate these experiments 'certainly enhanced the quality of the paper,' suggesting they were part of satisfactory revisions. OpenEval R3 includes C75 which peer R3 also addresses.

Strong agreement on lipidomics findings (C5-C7, C76-C88, C138-C141). Both support the phospholipid metabolism changes showing PE decrease and PG increase. OpenEval provides detailed assessment of the LC-MS methodology. Peer reviewers explicitly accept the 'decreased biosynthesis of unsaturated fatty acids and PE, along with an increase in the biosynthesis of PG.'

Both address fatty acid metabolism regulation at gene/protein level (C39-C49, C160-C161). OpenEval supports the multi-level evidence but notes modest sample size (n=4) and lack of Western blot quantification. Peer R6 groups these with broader molecular mechanism findings (C50-C60, C152-C154, C159, C162) and accepts them as part of the 'molecular mechanism underlying Mg2+-induced phenotypic resistance.'

Both address fatty acid degradation pathway downregulation (C50-C52, C159). OpenEval supports the qRT-PCR and Western blot data but notes the mechanistic link to magnesium is not established. Peer R6 accepts these as part of the overall molecular mechanism evidence without specific concerns.

Both address transcriptional regulation through fadR and fabR (C53-C60, C152-C154). OpenEval supports the genetic evidence but identifies an inconsistency: the claim that Mg2+ 'positively regulates fadR' (C153) contradicts decreased fadR expression data (C55, C57). Peer reviewers accept the molecular mechanism findings without raising this specific inconsistency.

Both address membrane potential/polarization (C8, C94-C96, C150). OpenEval supports the fluorescent dye measurements but identifies a critical inconsistency: the abstract claims magnesium 'increases membrane polarization' (C8) while results show 'depolarization' (C94). Peer R5 accepts the membrane biophysics findings, stating the study 'sheds light on...altering membrane composition, polarization and fluidity' without noting this contradiction.

Both address membrane fluidity and permeability (C9-C10, C97-C104, C151). OpenEval supports the fluorescent probe measurements and genetic validation with deletion mutants. Peer reviewers explicitly support these findings as demonstrating effects on 'membrane composition, polarization and fluidity which ultimately leads to antimicrobial resistance.'

Both address intracellular antibiotic accumulation (C11, C105-C109). OpenEval supports the direct measurements linking membrane properties to drug uptake with substantial effects (159-fold reduction). Peer R5 accepts these as part of the comprehensive membrane biophysics evidence without specific concerns.

Both address enzyme activity for phospholipid metabolism (C89-C91). OpenEval supports the enzyme-level evidence and notes the use of recombinant PSS demonstrates direct enzymatic effects, though lacks similar evidence for PGS. Peer R7 accepts these findings as part of the comprehensive approach 'spanning evaluation...to enzyme activity level evaluation.'

Both address PG biosynthesis mutants (C92-C93). OpenEval rates these as UNCERTAIN, noting the claims are correlative rather than causative and the inability to obtain Δpsd mutant prevents direct testing of PE's role. Peer R7 accepts the genetic findings without expressing uncertainty.

OpenEval R10 addresses PE inhibition inference (C145-C146) rating it UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing. Peer R8 also rates claims including C145-C146 as UNCERTAIN, noting 'the conclusions drawn by the authors are justified by the data, except for the interpretation of some experiments,' suggesting mechanistic interpretations may be overreaching. Both express similar reservations about inferential claims.

OpenEval R14 addresses whether magnesium effects are metabolically mediated (C75, C148), supporting the evidence but noting only one concentration was tested. Peer R3 groups C75 with functional validation experiments (C3-C4, C71-C74) and accepts them as part of satisfactory revisions without specific concerns about experimental design.

OpenEval R14 addresses metabolic mediation claim (C148), supporting it but suggesting multiple concentrations would strengthen conclusions. Peer R8 rates claims including C148 as UNCERTAIN, noting some interpretations may be overreaching, though accepts the underlying data.

Both address TCA cycle flux redirection (C149). OpenEval rates this UNCERTAIN, noting it's an inference lacking direct flux measurements (e.g., isotope tracing). Peer R8 also rates this UNCERTAIN, stating 'the conclusions drawn by the authors are justified by the data, except for the interpretation of some experiments.' Both agree this mechanistic interpretation is not definitively supported.
